lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Experience is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: The more recent Mobility Systems internship should appear before the Eastern Robotics role so recent work is easier to find.

items.says: Consider whether Education should appear before Experience.
items.because: Experience may deserve priority for roles emphasizing professional work.

items.says: Check whether a split “on-/call” produces malformed PDF text extraction.
items.because: A manual hyphen or line break could affect ATS parsing.

items.says: Verify that the contact link is real, clickable, and direct.
items.because: The example.com address should be replaced if it is literal rather than anonymized.

items.says: Clarify what owning the dashboards involved and what changed.
items.because: The bullet does not show an evidenced effect on reliability, incident response, or alert quality.

items.says: Clarify whether this on-call rotation is the one mentioned in the migration bullet.
items.because: The overlap is ambiguous.

items.says: Specify the workload or test conditions behind the p95 comparison.
items.because: Readers need to judge whether the before-and-after figures are comparable.

items.says: Clarify what “release cycles” measures and how the checks contributed to the change.
items.because: The two-weeks-to-three-days result needs to be easier to interpret and attribute.

items.says: Split or prioritize the migration, logging, onboarding, and on-call work.
items.because: The combined scope and causal link to the backlog outcome are hard to follow.

items.says: Measure the backlog or dispatch impact if possible.
items.because: That would make the migration’s scale and result easier to see.

items.says: Distinguish the weekend rotation from the earlier on-call reference if they differ.
items.because: The relationship between the two references is unclear.

items.says: Clarify what the triage branch does and how it screens the sensor signals.
items.because: The system’s role and the meaning of “case” may be unclear outside the domain.

items.says: State what the 68% backlog reduction is measured against.
items.because: The comparison is not specified.

items.says: Define the accuracy metric and, if possible, how the held-out set was constructed.
items.because: Readers need to know what “accuracy” means for this task.

items.says: Describe the gain as eight percentage points rather than an eight-percent relative gain.
items.because: The figures rise from 71% to 79%.

items.says: Contextualize “assistant-only loss masking” for broader audiences.
items.because: The specialized method may be opaque outside LLM-focused roles.

items.says: Clarify the workload, concurrency conditions, and comparison baseline for the latency result.
items.because: “Single-request” and “dynamic batching” can sound contradictory.

items.says: Contextualize INT8 where the audience may not know it.
items.because: Specialized abbreviations may obscure the key contribution.

items.says: Give the sentence a clear grammatical subject.
items.because: The opening phrase does not clearly say what reduced latency.

items.says: Define the scope and baseline of “end-to-end latency.”
items.because: The 5% result should be clear and measurable.

items.says: Contextualize GRPO and SFT where the audience may not know them.
items.because: Specialized abbreviations may obscure the key contribution.

items.says: Add evidence of what improved and how stability was assessed.
items.because: The bullet describes a method but not its effect.

items.says: Explain why one trajectory was sampled per prompt.
items.because: That choice may surprise technical readers.

items.says: Clarify what “them” refers to.
items.because: The reference may be unclear when the bullet is read on its own.

items.says: Give the number of reviewers or cases covered if known.
items.because: That would convey the runbook’s reach.

items.says: Identify whether the Agent Runtime Suite was personal, academic, open-source, or job-related.
items.because: “Owner” is otherwise difficult to interpret.

items.says: Substantiate or remove the generic adoption and delivery claims.
items.because: “Accelerating delivery and improving outcomes” gives no evidence of impact and dilutes stronger results.

items.says: The claimed 50% latency reduction is incorrect; 900 ms to 600 ms is 33.3%.
items.because: The inconsistency could undermine confidence in the other metrics.

items.says: Ensure the before-and-after p95 figures use the same workload and measurement setup.
The 71%-to-83% change is mislabeled as a 12% increase.
items.because: It is a 12-percentage-point increase, not a 12% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify the benchmark’s scope or size.
items.because: Readers need to judge how representative the result is.

items.says: Clarify whether you created, adapted, or contributed to the eight metrics.
items.because: Your role in the metrics is unclear.

items.says: Clarify what “upstreamed” means for acceptance or release, and verify the adoption status.
items.because: The claimed default-benchmark adoption should be accurate.

items.says: Specify that 0.89 is a Kendall correlation measure.
items.because: Readers need to understand what the number demonstrates.

items.says: Explain what “tracks injected degradation” means in the evaluation.
items.because: The result should not overstate what correlation proves.

items.says: Make the structural defects, instrumentation, and your role in their resolution more concrete.
items.because: The current terms are vague.

items.says: Consider trimming the bullet.
items.because: The other two bullets may already cover the contribution sufficiently.

items.says: Add relevant tools and technologies demonstrated in the experience bullets to Skills.
items.because: Omitting the specific systems behind several accomplishments makes the section less useful for matching roles.

items.says: Move Kubernetes out of “ML & Agents.”
items.because: It fits more naturally with infrastructure or deployment skills.

items.says: Support the Kubernetes skill elsewhere or remove it.
items.because: The work bullets do not show how you used it.

items.says: Contextualize GRPO where the audience may not know it.
items.because: Specialized abbreviations may be opaque outside LLM-focused roles.
